subject: writing sections of a document with stitch?

messages.author: 5f171faf83bd9c08
messages.subject: writing sections of a document with stitch?
parts:
There are multiple sections in my document that needs to perform the
same analysis followed by display of results on multiple data sources.

I could write a R functions that performs 1) analysis and 2) display
code. Then, do something like

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

\section{Analysis of data1}
<<>>=
a1 = analysis(data1)
display(a1)
@

\section{Analysis of data2}
<<>>=
a2 = analysis(data2)
display(a2)
@

...

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

But when there are many data sources, this gets messy really fast.

I feel like there should be a way to do this with code
externalization, but I don't see how.
stitch has this concept, but stitch works on standalone code only.

What would be the best way to repetitively perform this task?

Thanks!

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] writing sections of a document with stitch?
parts:
stitch() is supposed to run a single R script only; it is a
convenience function to do relatively simple jobs.

knit() is the real workhorse that you are supposed to use in the knitr
package, and you can see many examples under
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/master/inst/examples/, e.g.
knitr-manual.Rnw

code externalization is also one way to go; there are examples as
well: http://yihui.name/knitr/demo/externalization/

Regards,

messages.author: 5f171faf83bd9c08
messages.subject: Re: writing sections of a document with stitch?
parts:
As far as I can tell, the knitr can execute code in "chunks" and show
result inside a tex document.
What I would like to do is also generate some tex commands in these
"chunks".

To be more precise, I can probably do something like:

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
<<results=asis>>=
for (i in c(1:10)){
cat("\\section{Analysis of data",i,"}\n")
result = analysis(data[[1]])
display(result)
}
@
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

Then the display function has to be printing latex syntax.

I was wondering if there's a better way of automatically write latex
document sections, which includes some latex text + R code to be
executed.

If I am missing a crucial concept please forgive me.
A minimal example of how one would do this would be very helpful.

Thank you,

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Re: writing sections of a document with stitch?
parts:
OK, now I understand the problem better.

One way to do this is to write a small template which does the
analysis for your i-th dataset, and you can call knit() in a loop. I
have cooked up a minimal example at https://gist.github.com/2475551
The critical point is I have a global looping variable 'g', so the
template will give me different results according to the current value
of g.

Regards,
